title: Starter Code Sync Record
description: A record of a starter code synchronization run, stored in syncs/<assignment-id>/<sync-id>.json in the control repository.

sync_id.description: Unique timestamped identifier for this sync run.

synced_by.description: GitHub login of the lecturer who triggered the sync.

template_sha.description: Commit SHA from the template repository that was synchronized.

template_base_sha.description: That commit's parent. A student whose file still matches the base has not touched it, which is how the sync decides between writing to main and opening a pull request. Absent for a root commit.

selected_files.description: The paths actually applied. Previously the raw request, recorded as ['*'] while the operation merged the entire template tree regardless of what the lecturer had ticked.

status.description: Where the run is. `running` is written when it STARTS, and again as it goes, so a run that is cut off still leaves a record of who it reached; a record left at `running` whose run has ended is a run that died, which lib/sync-status.mjs asks the run itself about. `stopped` is the sync stopping itself at its time budget with `remaining` students not reached. ABSENT on records written before 2026-09-25, which were only ever written at the end, and means `completed`. No default, for the reason `per_student_range` gives.

run_id.description: The hub Actions run that did this sync - what a record left at `running` is checked against.

total_students.description: Repository records at the start, so a partial record says how far it got: `results` holds the ones reached.

remaining.description: Students not reached when it stopped. 0 on a completed run.

per_student_range.description: true: every student was sent what they were missing between their own starting point (`results[].from_sha`) and `template_sha`, not what one commit changed. Absent on records written before 2026-09-25, which are therefore NOT read as evidence of where a student is: one commit's files arriving is not holding that commit (lib/starter-sync.mjs `startingPointFor`). No default: a default would write `false` into every old record on validation, which is a different answer from absent only in wording, and a different one the day this is read.

all_files.description: Nothing was left out of the selection. Only then does a student this sync reached count as being at `template_sha` - a student who was not sent a file is not at the commit that changed it.

outcome.description: `merged-and-pr` exists because the clean/conflict split is per FILE: one sync can put three corrections straight onto a student's main and raise a pull request for the fourth. Such a student is counted in both auto_merged and pr_opened, so the summary counters deliberately do not sum to total.

files_merged.description: Files written directly to main because the student had not touched them.

files_conflicted.description: Files the student had changed, offered as a pull request instead.

from_sha.description: The template commit this student was synced FROM - their range started here. Null only when the template's head commit had no parent and nothing else was known.

from_source.description: How `from_sha` was known: an earlier per-student sync that reached them, the template commit whose tree their repository's first commit carries, or neither - in which case they were sent only this commit's changes, as every sync did before per-student ranges, and this record does not count as evidence of where they are.

files_kept.description: Files this commit ADDS that the student already has with other content - received earlier and worked in since - left alone rather than offered back as the starter version (lib/starter-sync.mjs `kept`).

issue_error.description: Why the notification issue could not be created. The issue IS how a student learns a starter-code pull request is waiting, so a failure to open one has to reach the record a lecturer reads - not just the run log.
